Biophysics.subject: Applied Sciences
Biophysics.question: The _____ was Interdisciplinary science.
Biophysics.fact: Biophysics is an interdisciplinary science that applies approaches and methods traditionally used in physics to study biological phenomena. Biophysics covers all scales of biological organization, from molecular to organismic and populations.

Booting process of Linux.fact: A hard disk to boot Linux stores the Master Boot Record (MBR), which contains the first-stage/primary bootloader in order to be loaded into RAM.

Booting process of Linux.subject: Applied Sciences
Booting process of Linux.question: In _____ systems, the Linux kernel can be executed directly by UEFI firmware via the EFI boot stub, but usually uses GRUB 2 or systemd-boot as a bootloader
Booting process of Linux.fact: In UEFI systems, the Linux kernel can be executed directly by UEFI firmware via the EFI boot stub, but usually uses GRUB 2 or systemd-boot as a bootloader. If UEFI Secure Boot is supported, a "shim" or "Preloader" is often booted by the UEFI before the bootloader or EFI-stub-bearing kernel.

Booting process of Linux.subject: Applied Sciences
Booting process of Linux.question: If UEFI _____ is supported, a "shim" or "Preloader" is often booted by the UEFI before the bootloader or EFI-stub-bearing kernel
Booting process of Linux.fact: If UEFI Secure Boot is supported, a "shim" or "Preloader" is often booted by the UEFI before the bootloader or EFI-stub-bearing kernel. Even if UEFI Secure Boot is disabled this may be present and booted in case it is later enabled.

Booting process of Linux.subject: Applied Sciences
Booting process of Linux.question: Even if UEFI _____ is disabled this may be present and booted in case it is later enabled
Booting process of Linux.fact: If UEFI Secure Boot is supported, a "shim" or "Preloader" is often booted by the UEFI before the bootloader or EFI-stub-bearing kernel. Even if UEFI Secure Boot is disabled this may be present and booted in case it is later enabled.

Booting process of Linux.subject: Applied Sciences
Booting process of Linux.question: The system startup stage on embedded Linux system starts by executing the firmware / program on the on-chip boot ROM, which then load bootloader / operating system from the storage device like eMMC, eUFS, _____, etc
Booting process of Linux.fact: The system startup stage on embedded Linux system starts by executing the firmware / program on the on-chip boot ROM, which then load bootloader / operating system from the storage device like eMMC, eUFS, NAND flash, etc.

Booting process of Linux.subject: Applied Sciences
Booting process of Linux.question: The on-chip boot ROM then loads the U-_____ into DRAM for the bootloader stage
Booting process of Linux.fact: The system startup stage on embedded Linux system starts by executing the firmware / program on the on-chip boot ROM, which then load bootloader / operating system from the storage device like eMMC, eUFS, NAND flash, etc. For example in a system with an i.MX7D processor and a bootable device which stores the OS (including U-Boot), the on-chip boot ROM sets up the DDR memory controller at first which allows the boot ROM's program to obtain the SoC configuration data from the external bootloade...

Booting process of Linux.subject: Applied Sciences
Booting process of Linux.question: Kernel image isn't an executable kernel, but a "compressed file" of the kernel instead, compressed into either z_____ or bzImage formats with zlib
Booting process of Linux.fact: The job of the second stage bootloader is to load the Linux kernel image into memory, and optional initial RAM disk. Kernel image isn't an executable kernel, but a "compressed file" of the kernel instead, compressed into either zImage or bzImage formats with zlib.

Booting process of Linux.subject: Applied Sciences
Booting process of Linux.question: In those systems, the first- and second-stage bootloaders are usually provided by the GRand Unified Bootloader (GRUB), and formerly provided by the _____ (LILO)
Booting process of Linux.fact: In those systems, the first- and second-stage bootloaders are usually provided by the GRand Unified Bootloader (GRUB), and formerly provided by the Linux Loader (LILO).

Booting process of Linux.subject: Applied Sciences
Booting process of Linux.question: The stage1 is loaded and executed by the _____ from the MBR
Booting process of Linux.fact: The stage1 is loaded and executed by the BIOS from the MBR.

Booting process of Linux.subject: Applied Sciences
Booting process of Linux.question: After a menu entry is chosen and optional parameters are given, _____ loads the linux kernel into memory and passes control to it
Booting process of Linux.fact: The second-stage loader (stage2, the /boot/grub/ files) is loaded by the stage1.5 and displays the GRUB startup menu that allows the user to choose an operating system or examine and edit startup parameters. After a menu entry is chosen and optional parameters are given, GRUB loads the linux kernel into memory and passes control to it.

Booting process of Linux.subject: Applied Sciences
Booting process of Linux.question: In _____ systems, the stage1 and stage1.5 usually are the same UEFI application file (such as grubx64.efi for x64 UEFI systems)
Booting process of Linux.fact: In UEFI systems, the stage1 and stage1.5 usually are the same UEFI application file (such as grubx64.efi for x64 UEFI systems). Beside GRUB, there are some more popular bootloaders: systemd-boot (formerly Gummiboot), a bootloader included with systemd that requires minimal configuration (for UEFI systems only).

Booting process of Linux.subject: Applied Sciences
Booting process of Linux.question: Beside GRUB, there are some more popular bootloaders: systemd-boot (formerly _____), a bootloader included with systemd that requires minimal configuration (for UEFI systems only)
Booting process of Linux.fact: Beside GRUB, there are some more popular bootloaders: systemd-boot (formerly Gummiboot), a bootloader included with systemd that requires minimal configuration (for UEFI systems only).

Booting process of Linux.question: rEFInd, a boot manager for _____ systems
Booting process of Linux.fact: rEFInd, a boot manager for UEFI systems. coreboot is a free implementation of the UEFI or BIOS and usually deployed with the system board, and field upgrades provided by the vendor if need be.

Booting process of Linux.subject: Applied Sciences
Booting process of Linux.question: coreboot is a free implementation of the _____ or BIOS and usually deployed with the system board, and field upgrades provided by the vendor if need be
Booting process of Linux.fact: rEFInd, a boot manager for UEFI systems. coreboot is a free implementation of the UEFI or BIOS and usually deployed with the system board, and field upgrades provided by the vendor if need be.

Booting process of Linux.subject: Applied Sciences
Booting process of Linux.question: Das U-_____ is a bootloader for embedded systems
Booting process of Linux.fact: rEFInd, a boot manager for UEFI systems. coreboot is a free implementation of the UEFI or BIOS and usually deployed with the system board, and field upgrades provided by the vendor if need be.

Booting process of Linux.fact: coreboot is a free implementation of the UEFI or BIOS and usually deployed with the system board, and field upgrades provided by the vendor if need be. Parts of coreboot becomes the systems BIOS and stays resident in memory after boot.

Booting process of Linux.subject: Applied Sciences
Booting process of Linux.question: It is used on systems that do not have a _____/UEFI but rather employ custom methods to read the bootloader into memory and execute it
Booting process of Linux.fact: coreboot is a free implementation of the UEFI or BIOS and usually deployed with the system board, and field upgrades provided by the vendor if need be. Parts of coreboot becomes the systems BIOS and stays resident in memory after boot.

Booting process of Linux.subject: Applied Sciences
Booting process of Linux.question: Historical bootloaders, no longer in common use, include: _____ does not understand or parse filesystem layout
Booting process of Linux.fact: Historical bootloaders, no longer in common use, include: LILO does not understand or parse filesystem layout. Instead, a configuration file (/etc/lilo.conf) is created in a live system which maps raw offset information (mapper tool) about location of kernel and ram disks (initrd or initramfs).

Booting process of Linux.subject: Applied Sciences
Booting process of Linux.question: The second-stage loader (stage2, the /boot/grub/ files) is loaded by the stage1._____ and displays the GRUB startup menu that allows the user to choose an operating system or examine and edit startup
Booting process of Linux.fact: The intermediate stage loader (stage1.5, usually core.img) is loaded and executed by the stage1 loader. The second-stage loader (stage2, the /boot/grub/ files) is loaded by the stage1.5 and displays the GRUB startup menu that allows the user to choose an operating system or examine and edit startup parameters.

Booting process of Linux.subject: Applied Sciences
Booting process of Linux.question: It also contains a command-line interface, which makes it easier to fix or modify _____ if it is misconfigured or corrupt
Booting process of Linux.fact: GRUB 1 includes logic to read common file systems at run-time in order to access its configuration file. This gives GRUB 1 ability to read its configuration file from the filesystem rather than have it embedded into the MBR, which allows it to change the configuration at run-time and specify disks and partitions in a human-readable format rather than relying on offsets.

Booting process of Linux.subject: Applied Sciences
Booting process of Linux.question: Loadlin is a bootloader that can replace a running DOS or _____ 9x kernel with the Linux kernel at run time
Booting process of Linux.fact: Loadlin is a bootloader that can replace a running DOS or Windows 9x kernel with the Linux kernel at run time. Another use case is when the Linux is located on a storage device which is not available to the BIOS for booting: DOS or Windows can load the appropriate drivers to make up for the BIOS limitation and boot Linux from there.

Booting process of Linux.subject: Applied Sciences
Booting process of Linux.question: For some platforms (like ARM 64-bit), kernel decompression has to be performed by the bootloader instead, like U-_____
Booting process of Linux.fact: For some platforms (like ARM 64-bit), kernel decompression has to be performed by the bootloader instead, like U-Boot. When its bzImage is invoked, function start() (of ./arch/i386/boot/head.S) is called to do some basic hardware setup then calls startup_32() (located in ./arch/i386/boot/compressed/head.S).

Booting process of Linux.subject: Applied Sciences
Booting process of Linux.question: When its bz_____ is invoked, function start() (of ./arch/i386/boot/head.S) is called to do some basic hardware setup then calls startup_32() (located in ./arch/i386/boot/compressed/head.S)
Booting process of Linux.fact: The kernel image is self-decompressed, which is a part of the kernel image's routine. When its bzImage is invoked, function start() (of ./arch/i386/boot/head.S) is called to do some basic hardware setup then calls startup_32() (located in ./arch/i386/boot/compressed/head.S).

Booting process of Linux.subject: Applied Sciences
Booting process of Linux.question: initrd usually contains the necessary modules needed to interface with storage peripherals, e.g _____ driver, and support a large number of possible hardware configurations
Booting process of Linux.fact: initrd usually contains the necessary modules needed to interface with storage peripherals, e.g SATA driver, and support a large number of possible hardware configurations.

Booting process of Linux.subject: Applied Sciences
Booting process of Linux.question: Finally, kernel_thread (in arch/i386/kernel/process.c) is called to start the _____ process (the first user-space process), and then starts the idle task via cpu_idle()
Booting process of Linux.fact: Many distributions use dracut to generate and maintain the initramfs image. Finally, kernel_thread (in arch/i386/kernel/process.c) is called to start the Init process (the first user-space process), and then starts the idle task via cpu_idle().

Booting process of Linux.subject: Applied Sciences
Booting process of Linux.question: Thus, the kernel stage initializes devices, mounts the root filesystem specified by the bootloader as read only, and runs Init (/sbin/init) which is designated as the first process run by the system (
Booting process of Linux.fact: Thus, the kernel stage initializes devices, mounts the root filesystem specified by the bootloader as read only, and runs Init (/sbin/init) which is designated as the first process run by the system (PID = 1).

Booting process of Linux.subject: Applied Sciences
Booting process of Linux.question: A message is printed by the kernel upon mounting the file system, and by _____ upon starting the Init process
Booting process of Linux.fact: Finally, kernel_thread (in arch/i386/kernel/process.c) is called to start the Init process (the first user-space process), and then starts the idle task via cpu_idle(). Thus, the kernel stage initializes devices, mounts the root filesystem specified by the bootloader as read only, and runs Init (/sbin/init) which is designated as the first process run by the system (PID = 1).

Booting process of Linux.subject: Applied Sciences
Booting process of Linux.question: Next, it initializes virtual devices related to the file system, such as LVM or software _____ before unmounting the initrd disk image and freeing up all the memory the disk image once occupied
Booting process of Linux.fact: Next, it initializes virtual devices related to the file system, such as LVM or software RAID before unmounting the initrd disk image and freeing up all the memory the disk image once occupied.

Booting process of Linux.subject: Applied Sciences
Booting process of Linux.question: Lennart Poettering and _____, software engineers that initially developed systemd, sought to surpass the efficiency of the init daemon in several ways
Booting process of Linux.fact: Lennart Poettering and Kay Sievers, software engineers that initially developed systemd, sought to surpass the efficiency of the init daemon in several ways.

Booting process of Linux.subject: Applied Sciences
Booting process of Linux.question: For inter-process communication, systemd makes _____ domain sockets and D-Bus available to the running daemons
Booting process of Linux.fact: For inter-process communication, systemd makes Unix domain sockets and D-Bus available to the running daemons.

Booting process of Windows.subject: Applied Sciences

Booting process of Windows.fact: The booting process of Microsoft Windows varies between different releases. It then loads WIN100.BIN or WIN200.BIN and WIN100.OVL or WIN200.OVL, along with the configuration settings file WIN.INI.

Booting process of Windows.subject: Applied Sciences
Booting process of Windows.question: The booting process of _____ varies between different releases
Booting process of Windows.fact: The booting process of Microsoft Windows varies between different releases.

Booting process of Windows.subject: Applied Sciences
Booting process of Windows.question: The default shell is the MS-DOS _____ (MSDOS.EXE)
Booting process of Windows.fact: The default shell is the MS-DOS Executive (MSDOS.EXE).

Booting process of Windows.subject: Applied Sciences
Booting process of Windows.question: The modules GDI.EXE, _____.EXE and USER.EXE, fonts, and the various device drivers (such as COMM.DRV, MOUSE.DRV, KEYBOARD.DRV) are incorporated in WIN100.BIN/WIN200.BIN and WIN100.OVL/WIN200.OVL
Booting process of Windows.fact: The modules GDI.EXE, KERNEL.EXE and USER.EXE, fonts, and the various device drivers (such as COMM.DRV, MOUSE.DRV, KEYBOARD.DRV) are incorporated in WIN100.BIN/WIN200.BIN and WIN100.OVL/WIN200.OVL.

Booting process of Windows.question: During the boot phase, _____.SYS and AUTOEXEC.BAT are executed, along with the configuration settings files WIN.INI and SYSTEM.INI
Booting process of Windows.fact: During the boot phase, CONFIG.SYS and AUTOEXEC.BAT are executed, along with the configuration settings files WIN.INI and SYSTEM.INI.

Booting process of Windows.subject: Applied Sciences
Booting process of Windows.question: Virtual device drivers are also loaded in the startup process: they are most commonly loaded from the registry (HKLM\System\_____ControlSet\Services\VxD) or from the SYSTEM.INI file
Booting process of Windows.fact: Virtual device drivers are also loaded in the startup process: they are most commonly loaded from the registry (HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services\VxD) or from the SYSTEM.INI file.

Booting process of Windows.subject: Applied Sciences
Booting process of Windows.question: In Windows 3.x, the WIN.COM starts _____.EXE (standard mode) or WIN386.EXE (386 enhanced mode)
Booting process of Windows.fact: In Windows 3.x, the WIN.COM starts DOSX.EXE (standard mode) or WIN386.EXE (386 enhanced mode). The DOSX.EXE (the standard mode kernel) later starts KRNL286.EXE (the Win16 API); the WIN386.EXE (the enhanced mode kernel) later starts KRNL386.EXE (the Win16 API in enhanced mode).

Booting process of Windows.subject: Applied Sciences
Booting process of Windows.question: The _____.EXE (the standard mode kernel) later starts KRNL286.EXE (the Win16 API); the WIN386.EXE (the enhanced mode kernel) later starts KRNL386.EXE (the Win16 API in enhanced mode)
Booting process of Windows.fact: In Windows 3.x, the WIN.COM starts DOSX.EXE (standard mode) or WIN386.EXE (386 enhanced mode). The DOSX.EXE (the standard mode kernel) later starts KRNL286.EXE (the Win16 API); the WIN386.EXE (the enhanced mode kernel) later starts KRNL386.EXE (the Win16 API in enhanced mode).

Booting process of Windows.subject: Applied Sciences
Booting process of Windows.question: Later, the _____ (PROGMAN.EXE) shell is started
Booting process of Windows.fact: Later, the Program Manager (PROGMAN.EXE) shell is started.

Booting process of Windows.subject: Applied Sciences
Booting process of Windows.question: The 32-bit VxD message server (MSGSRV32) starts MPREXE.EXE, which is responsible for loading the network logon client (such as Client for Microsoft Networks, Microsoft Family Logon or _____)
Booting process of Windows.fact: The 32-bit VxD message server (MSGSRV32) starts MPREXE.EXE, which is responsible for loading the network logon client (such as Client for Microsoft Networks, Microsoft Family Logon or Windows Logon).

Booting process of Windows.subject: Applied Sciences
Booting process of Windows.question: When a user is logging on to Windows, the startup sound is played, the shell (usually EXPLORER.EXE) is loaded from the [boot] section of the _____.INI file, and startup items are loaded
Booting process of Windows.fact: When all system configuration files and device drivers have been loaded, the 16-bit modules, KRNL386.EXE, GDI.EXE, and USER.EXE, are loaded, then the 32-bit DLLs (KERNEL32.DLL, GDI32.DLL, and USER32.DLL) are loaded. When a user is logging on to Windows, the startup sound is played, the shell (usually EXPLORER.EXE) is loaded from the [boot] section of the SYSTEM.INI file, and startup items are loaded.

Booting process of Windows.subject: Applied Sciences
Booting process of Windows.question: On the startup process, NK.BIN boot image or NK.EXE kernel is loaded by the _____ or EBOOT bootloader
Booting process of Windows.fact: On the startup process, NK.BIN boot image or NK.EXE kernel is loaded by the WCELDR or EBOOT bootloader.

Booting process of Windows.subject: Applied Sciences
Booting process of Windows.question: After the user has successfully logged into the machine, winlogon applies User and _____ setting and runs startup programs declared in the Windows Registry and in "Startup" folders
Booting process of Windows.fact: After the user has successfully logged into the machine, winlogon applies User and Computer Group Policy setting and runs startup programs declared in the Windows Registry and in "Startup" folders.

Booting process of Windows.subject: Applied Sciences
Booting process of Windows.question: Finally the Windows shell will be started; in _____ 3.x, the shell is usually Program Manager, and in Windows NT 4.0 and later, the shell is usually Windows Explorer
Booting process of Windows.fact: Finally the Windows shell will be started; in Windows NT 3.x, the shell is usually Program Manager, and in Windows NT 4.0 and later, the shell is usually Windows Explorer.

Bootloader.subject: Applied Sciences
Bootloader.question: The _____ was Software responsible for starting the computer.
Bootloader.fact: A bootloader, also spelled as boot loader or called bootstrap loader, is a computer program that is responsible for booting a computer and booting an operating system.

Bootloader.fact: The operating systems for S/360 through z/Architecture reside on direct access storage devices (DASDs), e.g., disk, drum.

Bootloader.fact: For these devices, Read IPL does a seek to cylinder 000016, head 000016, and orients to record 0116. For all supported operating systems, record 0116 contains a Read Data CCW to read a bootstrap record and a Transfer In Channel (TIC) CCW to the bootstrap.

Bootloader.subject: Applied Sciences
Bootloader.question: For all supported operating systems, record 0116 contains a _____ CCW to read a bootstrap record and a Transfer In Channel (TIC) CCW to the bootstrap
Bootloader.fact: For all supported operating systems, record 0116 contains a Read Data CCW to read a bootstrap record and a Transfer In Channel (TIC) CCW to the bootstrap.
